chapter.title: Stream Errors
chapter.para: As with any file or socket related function, an operation on a stream may fail for a variety of normal reasons (i.e.: Unable to connect to remote host, file not found, etc...). A stream related call may also fail because the desired stream is not registered on the running system. See the array returned by stream_get_wrappers for a list of streams supported by your installation of PHP. As with most PHP internal functions if a failure occurs an E_WARNING message will be generated describing the nature of the error.

section.title: Configuring error handling
section.simpara: As of PHP 8.6.0, the way stream errors are reported can be changed for every operation that uses a stream context, by setting the stream context options error_mode, error_store and error_handler. Each error is described by a StreamError object, whose code property is a StreamErrorCode case.

An error is either terminating, if it made the operation fail, such as a file that cannot be opened, or non-terminating, if the operation continued after reporting it. A single operation may report several errors.
The error_mode option takes a StreamErrorMode case and selects how errors are reported:

listitem.simpara: StreamErrorMode::Error, the default, emits diagnostics such as E_WARNING and E_NOTICE.
StreamErrorMode::Exception throws a StreamException if the operation reported a terminating error. Non-terminating errors do not throw and emit no diagnostics.
StreamErrorMode::Silent neither emits diagnostics nor throws.

section.simpara: The error_store option takes a StreamErrorStore case and selects which errors are kept for stream_last_errors. With the default, StreamErrorStore::Auto, this depends on the error mode:
The error_handler option is a callable that receives the list of StreamError objects of every operation that reported errors, regardless of the other two options.

note.simpara: These options cannot be set on the default context, so that code which does not pass a context keeps receiving diagnostics. They must be set on a context created with stream_context_create that is passed to the function, or that the stream was opened with.

section.simpara: See the stream context options for examples of each error mode and of an error handler.
